title: stateful-trajectory-sequencer-and-primed-warmup-checkpointer
content:
release_notes:
Adds a new deterministic workload runner that produces reproducible session trajectories and on-demand warmup checkpoints; no API breaking changes.

description:
Motivation: tail latency investigations for long-lived conversational workloads were hard to reproduce — transient priming paths and nondeterministic warmup order meant we could not reliably recreate the same KV cache state. This PR introduces a stateful trajectory sequencer runner that (1) deterministically schedules multi-turn sessions with configurable affinity and drift, (2) records compact warmup checkpoints (KV priming snapshots) and (3) provides a deterministic replay mode that applies checkpoints to reproduce tail events.

What I changed: single PR that implements the runner, checkpoint serialization, a small deterministic scheduler, and a reporting exporter that annotates traces with checkpoint IDs and session-affinity buckets. The runner supports: per-session seed, length distribution profiles, interleaving policies (round-robin, affinity-weighted, random-with-seed), and explicit checkpoint injection points. Checkpoints are small JSON blobs of token prefixes + KV metadata (non-sensitive) and an index file that maps checkpoint -> model-compatibility hints.

Why this matters: teams can now write golden reproducer harnesses for slow tails, instrument the warmup path, and share checkpoints between benchmark runs to compare kernel-level profiles with identical initial states. This reduces flakiness in perf regression triage and speeds up root cause analysis for divergence between model variants.

Testing and validation: unit tests added for scheduler determinism, checkpoint roundtrip, and export format. End-to-end synthetic runs on the benchmark cluster show p95/p99 stability when replaying the same checkpoint across 10 repeated runs: p95 variance < 2%, p99 variance < 5% (baseline without checkpointing had p99 variance ~18%). CI includes an integration job that runs a short deterministic scenario against a small local runtime container; flaky latency-test failed on first CI run due to a timing race and passed on retry.

How to use: util/bench/seq_runner --profile conversational_long --seed 42 --checkpoint-out=checkpoints/run-20260214.zip to record; util/bench/seq_runner --replay-checkpoint=checkpoints/run-20260214.zip --profile conversational_long --verify to run replay mode and emit a reproducible trace. Documentation updated in docs/benchmarking/seq-runner.md with example workflows and recommended profiles.

Migration/compatibility: no changes to public API surfaces used by customers. Checkpoint files are schema-versioned, and the runner will refuse to apply checkpoints incompatible with the target model (safety guard).

performance_summary:
Reproducer run (n=10) against local single-GPU runtime with model-x-quant: baseline replay disabled: p95 mean 78ms (var 1.8%), p99 mean 220ms (var 18%); with checkpoint replay enabled: p95 mean 76ms (var 1.2%), p99 mean 205ms (var 4.6%). Token throughput difference negligible (<1.5%).

review_comments:
Samir: Could we compress checkpoints with zstd to reduce S3 transfer? (suggested) — Author: added optional zstd flag and kept plain-json as default for debuggability.
Elena: Scheduler determinism looks good; please add a small fuzz test for seed collisions. — Author: added seed-collision test and fixed deterministic RNG seeding.
Tao: The reporter emits checkpoint IDs but not model hints; can we annotate compatibility info? — Author: added model-compatibility hint into checkpoint index and annotation in traces.
